history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration ensure that ICT assets are properly recorded in Umoja for greater visibility and reliability to ensure improved monitoring and controls.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure. United Nations entities are delegated the responsibility of managing all the assets (including ICT assets) that they control. Therefore, the responsibility of properly recording assets lies with the entities. The Office of Information and Communications Technology has demonstrated to the Board that it continues to update its Umoja records on the basis of the relevant guidance. The Office has taken the required action and demonstrated that its assets are now being recorded in line with the guidance.
history.board_assessment: Given that recent audit findings still reveal that the ICT assets are not being recorded with sufficient accuracy, the audit team considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that ICT assets are properly recorded in Umoja for greater visibility and reliability to ensure improved monitoring and controls.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Office of Information and Communications Technology at United Nations Headquarters works continuously with the Global Asset Management Policy Service and the Property Management and Inventory Control Unit to resolve Umoja record discrepancies. As the central equipment disposal hub at Headquarters, the Office receives returned assets, updates Umoja records and marks items as “Write off in process” (WRPR) for accurate tracking. Eligible equipment for donation is set to “idle” status with a notification reference; the remaining written-off assets are promptly disposed of and transferred to the staging area of the Property Management and Inventory Control Unit. The Office of Information and Communications Technology is committed to strengthening inventory record monitoring. The latest ICT asset report for authorization groups T00/T01, issued on 30 October 2025, confirms that there were no discrepancies. A new “Office responsible” field has also been added to clearly identify equipment maintained by the Office. Through this regular ongoing process – with proper Umoja recording, monitoring and discrepancy resolution – the recommendation is considered implemented.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office of Information and Communications Technology actively updates records for equipment for disposal and marks items in Umoja with “Write off in process” (WRPR) status to ensure accurate tracking, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
